# Investigative Report: Lazarus Group Links Between the Ronin Bridge and Harmony Horizon Bridge Thefts

## Executive Summary

This report examines whether the March 2022 Ronin Bridge theft and the June 2022 Harmony Horizon Bridge theft can be linked through public attribution, laundering patterns, and wallet evidence associated with North Korea’s Lazarus Group. The evidence supports a strong public attribution of both incidents to Lazarus Group, a North Korea-backed hacking organization. The Ronin attribution was publicly reinforced by the U.S. Treasury’s Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC), which identified the relevant Ethereum address as belonging to Lazarus Group. The FBI later confirmed that Lazarus Group was responsible for the Harmony Horizon Bridge theft. ([S3](https://www.elliptic.co/insights/540-million-stolen-from-the-ronin-defi-bridge); [S1](https://www.elliptic.co/insights/fbi-confirms-north-korea-s-lazarus-group-as-hackers-behind-100-million-harmony-horizon-bridge-theft))

The laundering evidence also provides a meaningful connection. Both thefts involved the rapid conversion or movement of stolen assets, intermediary wallets, and the use of Tornado Cash. Elliptic stated that the Harmony laundering pattern mirrored the laundering methods used by Lazarus Group after the Ronin theft. Chainalysis independently described a recurring North Korea-linked laundering sequence involving intermediary wallets, batch mixing through Tornado Cash, asset swaps, Bitcoin mixing, and eventual movement toward crypto-to-fiat cash-out services. ([S1](https://www.elliptic.co/insights/fbi-confirms-north-korea-s-lazarus-group-as-hackers-behind-100-million-harmony-horizon-bridge-theft); [S2](https://www.chainalysis.com/blog/axie-infinity-ronin-bridge-dprk-hack-seizure/))

The wallet evidence is directionally consistent but incomplete in the supplied material. The sources describe original theft wallets, intermediary wallets, Tornado Cash deposits and withdrawals, and a sanctioned Ethereum address associated with the Ronin exploiter. However, the provided information does not include the actual wallet addresses or transaction hashes. Accordingly, this report can establish an evidentiary relationship between the incidents at the attribution and behavioral-pattern level, but it cannot independently perform address-level verification from the supplied material.

The evidence does **not** independently establish that APT38 and Lazarus Group are identical organizational entities. The supplied sources use “Lazarus Group” and “North Korea-linked groups,” but do not mention APT38. Any equivalence between the two labels should therefore be treated as unverified within this evidence set.

## Scope, Method, and Source Reliability

The analysis uses only the four supplied source records. Duplicate copies of the same URLs were consolidated. The source identifiers used in this report are:

| Source ID | Publisher and date | Subject | Evidentiary value |
|---|---|---|---|
| S1 | Elliptic, May 9, 2023 | FBI confirmation of Lazarus attribution for the Harmony theft | High for public attribution and Harmony laundering analysis |
| S2 | Chainalysis, September 8, 2022 | Ronin laundering, seizures, and North Korea-linked activity | High for Ronin laundering and seizure information |
| S3 | Elliptic, March 29, 2022, updated April 14, 2022 | Ronin theft, OFAC attribution, and laundering | High for Ronin attribution and chronology |
| S4 | Elliptic, undated resource/index page | Elliptic research index | Low evidentiary value for the specific incidents; not relied upon for substantive findings |

The sources are commercial blockchain-intelligence publications. They are relevant because they report investigations based on blockchain tracing, but they are not equivalent to primary law-enforcement records. The strongest attribution evidence in the supplied material is the description of OFAC’s action regarding Ronin and the FBI confirmation concerning Harmony. The laundering-pattern analysis is based on Elliptic and Chainalysis investigative assessments and should be understood as expert analysis rather than independently reproduced forensic evidence.

## Incident Comparison

| Attribute | Ronin Bridge theft | Harmony Horizon Bridge theft |
|---|---|---|
| Date of theft | Approximately March 23, 2022; announced March 29 | June 24, 2022 |
| Reported assets | 173,600 ETH and 25.5 million USDC | Approximately $99.7 million in cryptoassets |
| Reported value | $540 million at the time of theft; over $615 million at discovery in the Elliptic account | Approximately $100 million |
| Attribution | Elliptic attributed the activity to Lazarus Group; OFAC later identified the exploiter address as Lazarus Group | FBI confirmed Lazarus Group responsibility; Elliptic said this confirmed its prior attribution |
| Exploitation method | Compromise of five of nine validator private keys; described as socially engineered | Source states that bridge over-centralization created vulnerability to social engineering, but does not provide a complete technical postmortem |
| Laundering indicators | Intermediary wallets, DEX conversion, centralized-exchange deposits, Tornado Cash, chain-hopping, Bitcoin-related laundering | Programmatic structuring, Tornado Cash, post-mixer withdrawals, later Railgun deposits, exchange deposits |
| Seizures or blocks | More than $30 million reported seized; approximately 10% of stolen funds by value | Binance and Huobi reportedly identified, blocked, and seized a portion |

The value differences should not be treated as contradictions in the underlying incident amounts. They reflect different valuation dates and reporting conventions. ([S2](https://www.chainalysis.com/blog/axie-infinity-ronin-bridge-dprk-hack-seizure/); [S3](https://www.elliptic.co/insights/540-million-stolen-from-the-ronin-defi-bridge); [S1](https://www.elliptic.co/insights/fbi-confirms-north-korea-s-lazarus-group-as-hackers-behind-100-million-harmony-horizon-bridge-theft))

## Public Attribution Evidence

### Ronin Bridge

The Ronin Network theft involved the withdrawal of 173,600 ETH and 25.5 million USDC. Elliptic reported that the bridge required five of nine validator approvals for funds to move and that the attacker obtained the private keys of five validators. Ronin’s postmortem, as summarized by Elliptic, assessed that the evidence pointed to a socially engineered attack rather than a technical flaw. ([S3](https://www.elliptic.co/insights/540-million-stolen-from-the-ronin-defi-bridge))

Elliptic initially linked the attack to Lazarus Group based on the victim context, the suspected social-engineering method, and the laundering pattern. On April 14, 2022, OFAC sanctioned the Ethereum address associated with the Ronin exploiter and identified its owner as Lazarus Group. This is the strongest explicit public attribution in the supplied Ronin material because it represents a government sanctions designation rather than only a private-sector assessment. ([S3](https://www.elliptic.co/insights/540-million-stolen-from-the-ronin-defi-bridge))

Chainalysis independently described the Ronin theft as a North Korea-linked incident and stated that its investigation traced stolen funds to cash-out points, contributing to the freezing or seizure of more than $30 million. It further characterized the theft as involving Lazarus Group. ([S2](https://www.chainalysis.com/blog/axie-infinity-ronin-bridge-dprk-hack-seizure/))

### Harmony Horizon Bridge

Elliptic reported that the Horizon Bridge was exploited on June 24, 2022, for approximately $99.7 million. The FBI later confirmed that Lazarus Group was behind the attack. Elliptic described the FBI announcement as confirming Elliptic’s earlier attribution, which had been based on similarities between the Harmony laundering activity and Lazarus Group’s previous blockchain laundering behavior. ([S1](https://www.elliptic.co/insights/fbi-confirms-north-korea-s-lazarus-group-as-hackers-behind-100-million-harmony-horizon-bridge-theft))

The source also states that concerns had previously been raised about the bridge’s centralization and vulnerability to social engineering. The article compares this concern with the Ronin incident, where the attacker obtained enough validator authority to authorize withdrawals. This similarity is relevant, but it is not conclusive proof that the same operators used the same initial-access technique in both cases. The supplied Harmony material does not provide the same level of technical detail about compromised keys or validator approvals as the Ronin source. ([S1](https://www.elliptic.co/insights/fbi-confirms-north-korea-s-lazarus-group-as-hackers-behind-100-million-harmony-horizon-bridge-theft); [S3](https://www.elliptic.co/insights/540-million-stolen-from-the-ronin-defi-bridge))

## Laundering-Pattern Linkage

The most significant connection between the two incidents is the reported similarity in laundering behavior.

For Ronin, Chainalysis described a five-stage North Korea-linked laundering technique:

1. Stolen Ether is transferred to intermediary wallets.
2. Ether is mixed in batches using Tornado Cash.
3. Ether is swapped for Bitcoin.
4. Bitcoin is mixed in batches.
5. Bitcoin is deposited with crypto-to-fiat services for cash-out.

Chainalysis also reported that the Ronin laundering operation involved more than 12,000 cryptocurrency addresses. After OFAC sanctioned Tornado Cash, Chainalysis observed Lazarus Group using decentralized finance services and cross-chain bridges to move between assets and blockchains. One cited example involved bridging ETH from Ethereum to BNB Chain, swapping ETH for USDD, and then bridging the resulting asset to the BitTorrent Chain. ([S2](https://www.chainalysis.com/blog/axie-infinity-ronin-bridge-dprk-hack-seizure/))

Elliptic’s Ronin analysis similarly reported that the stolen USDC was first swapped for ETH through decentralized exchanges, after which some ETH was deposited into centralized exchanges. When exchanges announced cooperation with law enforcement, the attacker shifted toward Tornado Cash. Elliptic reported that approximately $80.3 million in ETH had been sent through Tornado Cash by April 14, 2022, while approximately $9.7 million remained in intermediary wallets prepared for further laundering. ([S3](https://www.elliptic.co/insights/540-million-stolen-from-the-ronin-defi-bridge))

For Harmony, Elliptic reported that the stolen assets were programmatically structured through Tornado Cash. Elliptic specifically stated that the laundering methods mirrored those used by Lazarus Group in attempting to conceal the Ronin proceeds. The Harmony funds were subsequently withdrawn from Tornado Cash into several addresses, where they remained dormant until January 2023. ([S1](https://www.elliptic.co/insights/fbi-confirms-north-korea-s-lazarus-group-as-hackers-behind-100-million-harmony-horizon-bridge-theft))

In January 2023, Elliptic reported that the Harmony-linked funds were structured into deposits into Railgun, a privacy-oriented DeFi protocol. Elliptic estimated that approximately 70% of the Ether sent through Railgun to that point consisted of Harmony-hack funds. The article’s explanation is that a large share of one identifiable theft in a relatively small anonymity set can make mixing less effective. The funds were later deposited into three cryptoasset exchanges; Binance and Huobi reportedly identified, blocked, and seized part of the funds. ([S1](https://www.elliptic.co/insights/fbi-confirms-north-korea-s-lazarus-group-as-hackers-behind-100-million-harmony-horizon-bridge-theft))

The pattern linkage is therefore substantial:

| Pattern | Ronin | Harmony | Assessment |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| Intermediary wallets | Reported | Reported | Consistent |
| Tornado Cash use | Reported | Reported | Strong common indicator |
| Programmatic or batch structuring | Batch mixing and structured movements reported | Programmatic structuring reported | Consistent |
| Cross-chain or asset movement | DEX swaps and chain-hopping reported | Cross-chain bridge context and privacy-DeFi movement reported | Broadly consistent |
| Centralized-exchange exposure | Reported | Reported | Consistent |
| Post-sanctions migration from Tornado Cash | Noted through DeFi chain-hopping | Railgun use reported after Tornado Cash sanctions | Consistent evolution |

These similarities support the conclusion that the two incidents were operationally linked at the level of laundering methodology. They do not, by themselves, prove that every wallet or transaction was controlled by the same individuals.

## Wallet Evidence and Its Limits

The supplied sources refer to several classes of wallet evidence:

- A Ronin exploiter Ethereum address identified by OFAC as belonging to Lazarus Group.
- Original wallets holding stolen Ronin assets.
- Intermediary wallets used before or during laundering.
- Tornado Cash deposit and withdrawal addresses.
- Harmony-linked addresses that reportedly remained dormant after post-mixer withdrawals.
- Railgun deposit structures and later exchange deposits.
- More than 12,000 addresses used in the broader Ronin laundering operation.

However, the supplied material does not reproduce the actual hexadecimal wallet addresses, transaction IDs, block numbers, or an address-to-address transaction graph. This prevents a direct address-level comparison between the Ronin and Harmony thefts. It is therefore accurate to say that the sources report wallet tracing and attribution, but not that the supplied evidence independently demonstrates that a specific Ronin wallet directly funded a specific Harmony wallet.

The wallet evidence is strongest for the Ronin case because OFAC reportedly designated a specific Ethereum address. It is also significant for Harmony because Elliptic reported tracing the funds through Tornado Cash, Railgun, and exchanges. Nevertheless, the absence of address strings in the benchmark material requires caution about any claim of direct on-chain wallet continuity. ([S1](https://www.elliptic.co/insights/fbi-confirms-north-korea-s-lazarus-group-as-hackers-behind-100-million-harmony-horizon-bridge-theft); [S2](https://www.chainalysis.com/blog/axie-infinity-ronin-bridge-dprk-hack-seizure/); [S3](https://www.elliptic.co/insights/540-million-stolen-from-the-ronin-defi-bridge))

## Lazarus Group and APT38

The requested target refers to “Lazarus Group/APT38.” The supplied sources consistently identify Lazarus Group, North Korea-linked groups, or North Korean state hackers. None of the supplied source records mentions APT38. Consequently, this report cannot validate an organizational equivalence between Lazarus Group and APT38 using the permitted evidence.

The appropriate evidentiary formulation is:

> Both thefts are publicly attributed to Lazarus Group and North Korea-linked operators. The supplied evidence does not establish whether APT38 is an alternative name, a subordinate unit, an overlapping cluster, or a distinct entity.

Any stronger statement would exceed the source material.

## Findings

### Finding 1: Common public attribution

Both the Ronin Bridge and Harmony Horizon Bridge thefts were publicly attributed to Lazarus Group. Ronin attribution was reinforced by OFAC’s designation of the exploiter’s Ethereum address, while Harmony attribution was confirmed by the FBI. ([S1](https://www.elliptic.co/insights/fbi-confirms-north-korea-s-lazarus-group-as-hackers-behind-100-million-harmony-horizon-bridge-theft); [S3](https://www.elliptic.co/insights/540-million-stolen-from-the-ronin-defi-bridge))

### Finding 2: Common laundering methodology

The two incidents share reported use of intermediary wallets, structured transfers, Tornado Cash, and subsequent movement toward exchanges or other services. Elliptic explicitly characterized the Harmony laundering methods as mirroring those used after Ronin. ([S1](https://www.elliptic.co/insights/fbi-confirms-north-korea-s-lazarus-group-as-hackers-behind-100-million-harmony-horizon-bridge-theft); [S2](https://www.chainalysis.com/blog/axie-infinity-ronin-bridge-dprk-hack-seizure/); [S3](https://www.elliptic.co/insights/540-million-stolen-from-the-ronin-defi-bridge))

### Finding 3: Behavioral evolution after sanctions

The sources indicate that Tornado Cash sanctions were followed by greater use of DeFi services, chain-hopping, and Railgun. This suggests adaptation in laundering infrastructure, although the evidence does not prove that every subsequent transaction belonged to the same operator. ([S1](https://www.elliptic.co/insights/fbi-confirms-north-korea-s-lazarus-group-as-hackers-behind-100-million-harmony-horizon-bridge-theft); [S2](https://www.chainalysis.com/blog/axie-infinity-ronin-bridge-dprk-hack-seizure/))

### Finding 4: Direct wallet continuity is not demonstrated in the supplied material

The sources report wallet tracing but do not provide wallet addresses or transaction hashes in the information supplied. Direct wallet-to-wallet continuity between the two thefts therefore remains unverified here. ([S1](https://www.elliptic.co/insights/fbi-confirms-north-korea-s-lazarus-group-as-hackers-behind-100-million-harmony-horizon-bridge-theft); [S3](https://www.elliptic.co/insights/540-million-stolen-from-the-ronin-defi-bridge))

### Finding 5: APT38 linkage is unsupported

The supplied evidence does not mention APT38. The defensible conclusion is limited to Lazarus Group and North Korea-linked attribution. No APT38 equivalence should be asserted on this record.

## Conclusion

The evidence supports a concrete conclusion that the Ronin Bridge and Harmony Horizon Bridge thefts are linked through a common publicly attributed actor—Lazarus Group—and through a highly similar laundering playbook centered on intermediary wallets, structured asset movement, Tornado Cash, and later use of alternative DeFi privacy or chain-hopping mechanisms. The Ronin attribution has a particularly strong public basis because OFAC identified the relevant exploiter address as Lazarus Group. The Harmony attribution was subsequently confirmed by the FBI, and Elliptic expressly connected Harmony’s laundering behavior to the earlier Ronin pattern.

The evidence is sufficient to assess the two thefts as part of a Lazarus-linked campaign or activity set. It is not sufficient, from the supplied material alone, to establish direct wallet continuity, identify individual operators, or equate Lazarus Group with APT38. Those points remain uncertain and should not be presented as established facts.
